rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.2 and 3 - the study reports its own measurements (electrical parameters every 10 min, ultrasonic flowmeter discharges, pressure transducer) at the Tarazona de La Mancha pumping station during the 2004 season and calibrates a pumping-station efficiency model with them.
rows.notes: The study does not address the investment cost of on-demand networks nor the guarantee of supply during peak periods. It develops and calibrates a pumping-station energy model for a station serving an on-demand network and finds a 14% energy / 16% cost saving from changing the sequence of pump activation (variable speed pumps sequential instead of simultaneous). It reports the measured discharge distribution over the season (Fig. 9) but makes no comparison of on-demand with other delivery schedules and no statement on capital/investment cost of on-demand networks. Hence no own evidence on the claimed effect.

notes: Full text appears complete (pp. 479-486). Study is a single-season, single-pumping-station case study on energy efficiency; the citing passage attributes a claim about investment cost of on-demand networks that this paper does not examine.
